  "text": "But he knew her horn. She used it outside the swimming baths, where she waited with a towel spread over the passenger seat.

His mother turned toward the window.

“Don't look,” Anne said.

The younger father straightened without the key. There was a pale mark on his palm where it had been.

“Is she alone?” he asked.

“No one is alone in there.”

The boy worked at a knot with his thumbnail. It was hard and greasy, like something caught in a comb.

“Careful,” said the older father.

The knot opened.

Warm air touched the boy's face. He smelled chlorine and the chocolate biscuits his grandmother kept in the glove compartment. For a moment his hair was wet.

Then he was standing in the hall again, holding the thread.

His mother caught his wrist.

“What did you lose?”

He looked down. Both shoes were there. His trousers had their usual knees.

“Nothing.”

“Tell me your teacher's name.”

He knew her room, the red watch she took off before washing the paint pots. He knew she laughed without showing her teeth.

His mouth stayed open.

Anne sat back on her heels.

Outside, the horn sounded once.

The older father went to the door and laid his forehead against it.

“I can take him,” he said.

His mother tightened her grip.

“You did.”

The boy let go of the loosened knot. He wanted his schoolbag now, urgently: his name was written inside it, and there were things he had put there himself.

From upstairs came the scrape of a bed being dragged across the floor."
